glossary.text: India's law on how personal data in digital form may be collected and used, made up of the DPDP Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025. Its main duties on hospitals take effect on 13 May 2027.
The person the personal data is about, such as a patient or an employee. For a child, it includes the parent or lawful guardian.
The organisation that decides why and how personal data is processed. A hospital is the Data Fiduciary for its patients' and employees' data.

A Data Fiduciary the Central Government notifies as significant because of the volume and sensitivity of data it handles. It has extra duties: a Data Protection Officer in India, an independent data auditor and yearly impact assessments.
An outside party that processes personal data for the hospital, such as a hosting provider or a reference laboratory. The hospital stays accountable for what its processors do.

The person who answers Data Principals' questions about processing and oversees privacy compliance. Only a Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint one; other hospitals name a privacy lead or contact person.
The body set up under the DPDP Act to receive breach intimations, hear complaints and impose penalties. A Data Principal goes to the hospital's grievance route first.
A company registered with the Data Protection Board through which a person can give, review and withdraw consent across organisations. A hospital may receive consent through one.
Any data about an individual who can be identified by it or in relation to it. In a hospital this covers patient identity, clinical records, staff records and visitor footage.

Unauthorised processing, disclosure, alteration or loss of personal data that compromises its confidentiality, integrity or availability. The decision to notify is made and approved by an authorised person, never by the system.
The ground that allows a processing activity: the person's consent, or one of the legitimate uses the Act lists. Each activity in the processing register records its basis.
A purpose for which the Act allows processing without consent, such as data a patient gives voluntarily for treatment, a medical emergency, employment or a legal duty.
The statement given to a person that says what data is collected, why, and how to exercise rights and complain. Each version is kept so auditors can see which one applied.
The term ISO standards use for personal data. Annex A control 5.34 covers privacy and protection of PII.
A structured review of the risks a processing activity poses to the people whose data it uses, and how they are managed. It is mandatory yearly for a Significant Data Fiduciary.
A requirement that has been published but does not apply until a later date. It is listed and assessed separately as readiness, and is never mixed into the score for requirements in force.
The body that publishes international standards. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 sets the requirements for an information security management system.
The policies, roles, risk process and controls an organisation uses to manage information security in a planned way. ISO/IEC 27001 defines what it must contain.
The document that lists every Annex A control, says whether the hospital needs it and why, and records its implementation status. Each approved version is kept.

The list of 93 reference controls at the back of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, in four themes: organizational, people, physical and technological. Every one must be accounted for in the Statement of Applicability.
The person accountable for information security. In many hospitals the IT head holds this role.
Signing in with a second proof, such as a code from a phone app, as well as a password. Here it is called two-step sign-in.
Giving access according to a person's role rather than person by person. In this product a role sets what each module allows, narrowed further by hospital, department and audit assignment.
Signing in once through the organisation's identity system instead of a separate password for each application.
Technical testing that looks for security weaknesses and tries to exploit them. This product records the results of approved tests; it does not run intrusive tests itself.
The national agency for cyber security incidents. Its directions require certain cyber incidents to be reported within six hours of being noticed.
The longest a system may be down after a failure before the harm is unacceptable. The requirements document sets an initial target of 4 hours for this product.
The most data, measured in time, that may be lost in a failure. The requirements document sets an initial target of 1 hour for this product.
A system that collects security logs from many sources and raises alerts. Incidents can be fed from it.
The systems that create user identities and control what each can reach. It supplies information for access reviews.
Reading the words in a scanned page or photograph so they can be searched. It is used on evidence documents.
The level of a risk before any controls are taken into account, scored as likelihood multiplied by impact on scales of 1 to 5.
The level of a risk that remains after controls. A low residual score does not accept the risk: acceptance needs approval by an authorised person.
The decision about what to do with a risk: modify it with controls, retain it, avoid it or share it. Treatment actions are tracked to completion.
The combined practice of directing an organisation, managing what could go wrong, and proving that laws and standards are followed.
The action taken to fix a problem that was found and to stop it happening again. Closure needs implementation evidence and an effectiveness check by someone other than the owner or implementer.
A requirement that is not met. A major nonconformity is a failure that undermines the system or the requirement as a whole; a minor one is a lapse that does not.
Something the auditor noticed that is not a nonconformity today but could become one, or the record of what was found in a test.
The recorded result of comparing what the auditor saw with the audit criterion. A finding keeps the link to the test it came from.
The requirement an audit test is judged against, such as a section of the Act or an ISO clause, in a specific framework version.
The auditor's record of a test: what was examined, the sample, the result and the reviewer. Only auditors assigned to the audit can see them.
A measure the hospital operates to meet a requirement or reduce a risk. One control can be mapped to several requirements across frameworks, so its evidence is collected once.
A document or record that shows a control operates. Uploading it proves nothing until a reviewer who did not submit it has accepted it.
Whether a requirement applies to a particular hospital. A not-applicable decision needs a written justification and approval, and can be reassessed when operations or the law change.
Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant.
A measure of how well something is working. Each one here shows its calculation rule on hover.
Software provided over the internet for a subscription rather than installed by each customer.
A consultant running assessments and audits for several hospitals from one account. Each consultant sees only the hospitals assigned to them.
One customer organisation on a shared installation. Each tenant's data is kept apart from every other tenant's.
The main system for registration, admissions, billing and orders. It is also written HIMS, Hospital Information Management System.
Another name for the hospital information system.
The digital clinical record kept by one hospital for its patients.
A patient's health record designed to be shared across providers. In everyday use it overlaps with the electronic medical record.
The system that manages laboratory orders, samples and results.
The system that stores and displays radiology images such as X-rays, CT and MRI scans.

glossary.full: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine
glossary.text: The standard format and protocol for medical images. Imaging machines use it to send studies to the PACS.
A family of standards for exchanging clinical and administrative data between health systems.
The modern HL7 standard for exchanging health data over web interfaces.
The system of record for employees. It supplies joiner and leaver information for access reviews.
The finance and purchasing system of record. It can supply vendor and contract information.
The number a hospital gives each patient. Records in this product refer to people by reference numbers, not names.
The national health account number under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, used to link a person's health records across providers.

glossary.full: National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers
glossary.text: India's accreditation body for hospitals. This product does not issue accreditation; the same control and evidence structure can be reused for it later.

glossary.full: National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories
glossary.text: India's accreditation body for laboratories.
An international body that accredits hospitals.
A company that processes health insurance claims for insurers. Hospitals share patient and billing data with it for cashless treatment.
A defined way for one system to exchange data with another.
The standard for sending email. Notifications can be emailed when a mail server is configured.
A standard for passing user account information between systems.
The standard used for single sign-on with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Okta.

agents.name: Document analysis
agents.does: Reads an evidence document, identifies the requirements it is relevant to, suggests control mappings and retrieves similar evidence already on file.

agents.name: Gap identification
agents.does: Looks across a hospital's applicable requirements for missing controls, missing or expired evidence, failed tests and recorded gaps.

agents.name: Audit observation drafting
agents.does: Drafts the wording of an audit observation from the criterion, the sample and the auditor's notes.

agents.name: Corrective action suggestions
agents.does: Suggests lines of enquiry for root cause and possible corrective actions for a finding, drawing on similar earlier actions.

agents.name: Audit report drafting
agents.does: Drafts the audit report from the audit's scope, criteria, test results and findings.

agents.name: Control mapping suggestions
agents.does: Suggests which existing controls address a requirement, for review mapping by mapping.

requirement.description: Personal data processed in India or in connection with offering goods or services in India is transferred abroad only in line with requirements the Central Government specifies.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Data flow register; transfer assessments

_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Publish how rights are exercised and answer grievances in time
requirement.description: The means of making a rights request and the identifiers needed are published, and the grievance system responds within a reasonable period that does not exceed ninety days.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Published rights procedure; request turnaround figures

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Carry out the yearly assessment and audit of a Significant Data Fiduciary, if notified
requirement.description: A Significant Data Fiduciary carries out a data protection impact assessment and an audit every twelve months and reports the significant observations to the Board.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Impact assessment and audit reports; notification status

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Use the children's data exemptions only as prescribed
requirement.description: The exemptions for certain fiduciaries and purposes, including health services provided by clinical establishments and health professionals, apply only to the extent needed to protect the child's health.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Documented reliance on the exemption for paediatric care

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Verify the lawful guardian of a person with a disability
requirement.description: Due diligence confirms that the person giving consent is the guardian appointed under the applicable guardianship law.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Guardian verification procedure and records

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Verify the parent's identity and age before processing a child's data
requirement.description: Appropriate measures confirm that the person giving consent for a child is an identifiable adult who is the parent.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Guardian verification procedure and records

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Display the contact for questions on the website or app
requirement.description: The business contact of the Data Protection Officer or responsible person is shown prominently on the website or app and in every reply to a Data Principal.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Screenshots of website, app and response templates

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Keep to the retention and erasure rules, including log retention
requirement.description: Personal data is erased once the purpose is no longer served unless a law requires it to be kept, and personal data and processing logs are kept for at least one year for the purposes the Rules specify.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Retention schedule; log retention settings; erasure records

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Report a breach to affected people and the Board in the set form and time
requirement.description: Affected Data Principals are told without delay what happened, the likely consequences and what to do. The Board is told without delay, with a detailed report within seventy-two hours unless it allows longer.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Breach procedure; notification records with times

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Apply the minimum security safeguards
requirement.description: Safeguards include securing data by measures such as encryption or masking, controlling access, keeping and reviewing logs, backups for continued processing, retaining logs for one year, and contract terms that bind processors.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Encryption, access control, logging, backup and processor contract evidence

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Make the notice clear, standalone and itemised
requirement.description: The notice can be understood on its own, lists the personal data and the specific purpose in plain language, and gives the link or means to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board.
requirement.guidance: Rule 1 brings Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 into force eighteen months after publication (13 May 2027). Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Notice review against each element

_labels.framework: FW-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
_labels.version: FV-0002 · Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))

requirement.title: Follow any restriction on transfers outside India
requirement.description: Personal data may be transferred outside India except to countries the Central Government restricts by notification.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Data flow register showing destinations outside India

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Let Data Principals nominate someone to act for them
requirement.description: A Data Principal can nominate another person to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Nomination procedure and records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Give ready access to grievance redressal
requirement.description: Grievances are answered within the prescribed period. The Data Principal uses this route before approaching the Board.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Grievance timelines and escalations

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Correct, complete, update and erase on request
requirement.description: On request, inaccurate data is corrected, incomplete data completed and data updated, and data is erased unless it must be kept for the purpose or by law.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Correction and erasure requests with outcome and any legal retention reason

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Give Data Principals access to information about their data
requirement.description: On request, a Data Principal is given a summary of the personal data processed, the processing carried out, and who the data has been shared with.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Access requests and responses

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Meet the extra duties of a Significant Data Fiduciary, if notified
requirement.description: A fiduciary notified as significant appoints a Data Protection Officer based in India and an independent data auditor, and carries out impact assessments and periodic audits.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Notification status; DPO appointment; impact assessment and audit reports

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Do not process children's data in harmful ways
requirement.description: Processing likely to harm a child's well-being is not undertaken, and children are not tracked, behaviourally monitored or targeted with advertising, subject to the exemptions prescribed.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Assessment of paediatric and school-health processing

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Get verifiable consent of a parent or guardian for children
requirement.description: Before processing the personal data of a child, or of a person with a disability who has a lawful guardian, verifiable consent of the parent or guardian is obtained, subject to the exemptions prescribed.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Paediatric registration process; guardian consent records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Run an effective grievance redressal mechanism
requirement.description: There is an effective way for Data Principals to raise grievances and have them redressed.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Grievance procedure; rights and grievance register

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Publish a contact for questions about processing
requirement.description: The business contact of the Data Protection Officer, or of a person who can answer questions about processing, is published.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Website and notice showing the contact

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Erase personal data when it is no longer needed
requirement.description: Personal data is erased when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served, unless a law requires it to be kept, and processors are made to erase it too.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Retention schedule with legal basis; erasure records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Tell the Board and affected people about a personal data breach
requirement.description: On a personal data breach, the Data Protection Board and each affected Data Principal are informed in the prescribed form and manner.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Incident register with notification decisions, approvals and timestamps

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Protect personal data with reasonable security safeguards
requirement.description: Personal data held by the hospital or its processors is protected by reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Security controls, technical assessments, access reviews

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Put technical and organisational measures in place
requirement.description: Appropriate technical and organisational measures are implemented so the Act is observed in practice.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Policies, roles, training records and control register

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Keep personal data accurate and complete where it drives decisions
requirement.description: Where personal data is used to make a decision about the Data Principal or is disclosed to another fiduciary, reasonable effort is made to keep it complete, accurate and consistent.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Data quality checks on patient master and clinical records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Engage processors only under a valid contract
requirement.description: A Data Processor is appointed only under a valid contract.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Processor contracts and data protection addenda

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Stay accountable for processing done by processors
requirement.description: The hospital remains responsible for complying with the Act for processing done on its behalf by a Data Processor.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Vendor register identifying processors; oversight records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Rely on a legitimate use only where the Act allows it
requirement.description: Processing without consent is limited to the legitimate uses listed, such as data given voluntarily for a stated purpose, a medical emergency, employment and legal obligations.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Processing register showing which legitimate use applies and why

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Be able to prove notice and consent
requirement.description: If consent is the ground relied on, the hospital must be able to show that notice was given and consent obtained.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Consent records with timestamp, notice version and proof

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Make withdrawal of consent as easy as giving it
requirement.description: A Data Principal can withdraw consent at any time, as easily as it was given. Processing based on it then stops within a reasonable time, including at processors.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Withdrawal procedure; withdrawal events and the action taken on each

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Ask for consent in clear and plain language
requirement.description: The consent request is in plain language, is available in English or a scheduled Indian language, and gives the contact for questions.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Consent request wording in each language offered

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Obtain consent that is free, specific, informed and unambiguous
requirement.description: Consent is a clear affirmative action for a specified purpose, and covers only the personal data needed for that purpose.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Consent forms and screens; sample consent records

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Give notice with or before every consent request
requirement.description: A request for consent comes with a notice saying what personal data is collected and why, how to exercise rights and how to complain to the Data Protection Board.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Privacy notices in use, with versions and the channels where they are given

_labels.framework: FW-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
_labels.version: FV-0001 · Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

requirement.title: Process personal data only on a lawful ground
requirement.description: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose, either with the Data Principal's consent or for one of the legitimate uses the Act lists.
requirement.guidance: Operative provisions of the Act take effect on 13 May 2027 under the phased commencement notified on 13 November 2025. Confirm against the Gazette.
requirement.evidence_expected: Processing register showing the ground relied on for each activity

training_programme.title: Information security awareness for hospital staff
training_programme.description: Starter programme. Replace the questions with your own.

questions.q: You step away from the nursing station computer for a few minutes. What should you do?
options: Leave it, you will be back soon
Ask a visitor to watch it

questions.q: A colleague asks to use your HIS login because theirs is locked. What is correct?
options: Share it, patient care comes first
Refuse and help them get their own access restored
Write the password on a note for them
Log in for them and walk away

questions.q: An email asks you to confirm your password to keep your mailbox active. What is it most likely to be?
options: A system test you can ignore silently

training_programme.title: Patient privacy and the DPDP Act: the essentials
training_programme.description: Starter programme. Replace the questions with your own.

questions.q: A patient's relative asks at the nursing station for a copy of the patient's reports. What do you do first?
options: Hand them over, they are family
Confirm the patient has authorised it, following the hospital procedure

questions.q: Which of these is personal data?
options: The number of beds in the ward
A patient's UHID with their diagnosis

questions.q: A patient wants to withdraw consent to receive health camp messages. Who can record it?
options: It is logged as a consent withdrawal and acted on by the owner of that processing

questions.q: You sent a discharge summary to the wrong email address. What should you do?
options: Wait and see if anyone notices
Report it at once as an incident
Delete the sent mail and move on
Ask the recipient to ignore it and tell nobody

items.report:
AUDIT REPORT (DRAFT): Integrated DPDP readiness and ISO 27001 internal audit FY 2026-27
Project HSP-0001/2026/AUD-0002 · Kaveri Multispeciality Hospital · Integrated DPDP and ISO 27001

1. Objectives
Assess readiness for the DPDP Act and Rules before they take effect, and conformity of the ISMS with ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

2. Scope and exclusions
All clinical and support departments at the main campus, the central laboratory and the hospital data centre.
Exclusions: Velachery outpatient clinic (next cycle); research registry.

3. Audit criteria
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems (2022)
- Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)))
- Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023)

4. Work performed
150 audit tests planned: 50 passed, 8 failed, 0 not applicable, 92 not yet tested. 41 have been reviewed and approved.

5. Findings
3 minor nonconformity, 1 observation, 3 major nonconformity.
5.1 FND-0007 [Minor nonconformity] ISO 27001 A.8.8: Vulnerability management review: test failed
    9 critical findings older than 30 days, 3 on internet-facing systems.
5.2 FND-0006 [Observation] ISO 27001 A.7.7: A.7.7 Clear desk and clear screen: test failed
    At 6 of 10 nursing stations visited, screens were unlocked and unattended.
5.3 FND-0005 [Minor nonconformity] ISO 27001 A.8.22: A.8.22 Segregation of networks: test failed
    MRI and CT consoles sit on the same network segment as general workstations.
5.4 FND-0004 [Major nonconformity] ISO 27001 A.5.18: A.5.18 Access rights: test failed
    Quarterly access review covered the HIS only. 4 of 25 sampled leavers still had active LIS or PACS accounts.
5.5 FND-0003 [Major nonconformity] DPDP Act S.16: S.16 Follow any restriction on transfers outside India: test failed
    Imaging studies are reported by radiologists outside India. No record of where, and no assessment of the transfer.
5.6 FND-0002 [Minor nonconformity] DPDP Rules Rule 8: Rule 8 Keep to the retention and erasure rules, including log retention: test failed
    Access logs of the HIS are retained for 90 days; LIS and PACS logs for 30 days.
5.7 FND-0001 [Major nonconformity] DPDP Act S.8(2): S.8(2) Engage processors only under a valid contract: test failed
    Two processors (teleradiology and SMS gateway) process patient data without a contract containing data protection terms.

6. Conclusion
To be written by the lead auditor. This draft states what the records show and gives no audit opinion.

glossary.text: India's law on how personal data in digital form may be collected and used, made up of the DPDP Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025. Its main duties on hospitals take effect on 13 May 2027.
The person the personal data is about, such as a patient or an employee. For a child, it includes the parent or lawful guardian.
The organisation that decides why and how personal data is processed. A hospital is the Data Fiduciary for its patients' and employees' data.

A Data Fiduciary the Central Government notifies as significant because of the volume and sensitivity of data it handles. It has extra duties: a Data Protection Officer in India, an independent data auditor and yearly impact assessments.
An outside party that processes personal data for the hospital, such as a hosting provider or a reference laboratory. The hospital stays accountable for what its processors do.

The person who answers Data Principals' questions about processing and oversees privacy compliance. Only a Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint one; other hospitals name a privacy lead or contact person.
The body set up under the DPDP Act to receive breach intimations, hear complaints and impose penalties. A Data Principal goes to the hospital's grievance route first.
A company registered with the Data Protection Board through which a person can give, review and withdraw consent across organisations. A hospital may receive consent through one.
Any data about an individual who can be identified by it or in relation to it. In a hospital this covers patient identity, clinical records, staff records and visitor footage.

Unauthorised processing, disclosure, alteration or loss of personal data that compromises its confidentiality, integrity or availability. The decision to notify is made and approved by an authorised person, never by the system.
The ground that allows a processing activity: the person's consent, or one of the legitimate uses the Act lists. Each activity in the processing register records its basis.
A purpose for which the Act allows processing without consent, such as data a patient gives voluntarily for treatment, a medical emergency, employment or a legal duty.
The statement given to a person that says what data is collected, why, and how to exercise rights and complain. Each version is kept so auditors can see which one applied.
The term ISO standards use for personal data. Annex A control 5.34 covers privacy and protection of PII.
A structured review of the risks a processing activity poses to the people whose data it uses, and how they are managed. It is mandatory yearly for a Significant Data Fiduciary.
A requirement that has been published but does not apply until a later date. It is listed and assessed separately as readiness, and is never mixed into the score for requirements in force.
The body that publishes international standards. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 sets the requirements for an information security management system.
The policies, roles, risk process and controls an organisation uses to manage information security in a planned way. ISO/IEC 27001 defines what it must contain.
The document that lists every Annex A control, says whether the hospital needs it and why, and records its implementation status. Each approved version is kept.

The list of 93 reference controls at the back of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, in four themes: organizational, people, physical and technological. Every one must be accounted for in the Statement of Applicability.
The person accountable for information security. In many hospitals the IT head holds this role.
Signing in with a second proof, such as a code from a phone app, as well as a password. Here it is called two-step sign-in.
Giving access according to a person's role rather than person by person. In this product a role sets what each module allows, narrowed further by hospital, department and audit assignment.
Signing in once through the organisation's identity system instead of a separate password for each application.
Technical testing that looks for security weaknesses and tries to exploit them. This product records the results of approved tests; it does not run intrusive tests itself.
The national agency for cyber security incidents. Its directions require certain cyber incidents to be reported within six hours of being noticed.
The longest a system may be down after a failure before the harm is unacceptable. The requirements document sets an initial target of 4 hours for this product.
The most data, measured in time, that may be lost in a failure. The requirements document sets an initial target of 1 hour for this product.
A system that collects security logs from many sources and raises alerts. Incidents can be fed from it.
The systems that create user identities and control what each can reach. It supplies information for access reviews.
Reading the words in a scanned page or photograph so they can be searched. It is used on evidence documents.
The level of a risk before any controls are taken into account, scored as likelihood multiplied by impact on scales of 1 to 5.
The level of a risk that remains after controls. A low residual score does not accept the risk: acceptance needs approval by an authorised person.
The decision about what to do with a risk: modify it with controls, retain it, avoid it or share it. Treatment actions are tracked to completion.
The combined practice of directing an organisation, managing what could go wrong, and proving that laws and standards are followed.
The action taken to fix a problem that was found and to stop it happening again. Closure needs implementation evidence and an effectiveness check by someone other than the owner or implementer.
A requirement that is not met. A major nonconformity is a failure that undermines the system or the requirement as a whole; a minor one is a lapse that does not.
Something the auditor noticed that is not a nonconformity today but could become one, or the record of what was found in a test.
The recorded result of comparing what the auditor saw with the audit criterion. A finding keeps the link to the test it came from.
The requirement an audit test is judged against, such as a section of the Act or an ISO clause, in a specific framework version.
The auditor's record of a test: what was examined, the sample, the result and the reviewer. Only auditors assigned to the audit can see them.
A measure the hospital operates to meet a requirement or reduce a risk. One control can be mapped to several requirements across frameworks, so its evidence is collected once.
A document or record that shows a control operates. Uploading it proves nothing until a reviewer who did not submit it has accepted it.
Whether a requirement applies to a particular hospital. A not-applicable decision needs a written justification and approval, and can be reassessed when operations or the law change.
Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant.
A measure of how well something is working. Each one here shows its calculation rule on hover.
Software provided over the internet for a subscription rather than installed by each customer.
A consultant running assessments and audits for several hospitals from one account. Each consultant sees only the hospitals assigned to them.
One customer organisation on a shared installation. Each tenant's data is kept apart from every other tenant's.
The main system for registration, admissions, billing and orders. It is also written HIMS, Hospital Information Management System.
Another name for the hospital information system.
The digital clinical record kept by one hospital for its patients.
A patient's health record designed to be shared across providers. In everyday use it overlaps with the electronic medical record.
The system that manages laboratory orders, samples and results.
The system that stores and displays radiology images such as X-rays, CT and MRI scans.

glossary.full: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine
glossary.text: The standard format and protocol for medical images. Imaging machines use it to send studies to the PACS.
A family of standards for exchanging clinical and administrative data between health systems.
The modern HL7 standard for exchanging health data over web interfaces.
The system of record for employees. It supplies joiner and leaver information for access reviews.
The finance and purchasing system of record. It can supply vendor and contract information.
The number a hospital gives each patient. Records in this product refer to people by reference numbers, not names.
The national health account number under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, used to link a person's health records across providers.

glossary.full: National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers
glossary.text: India's accreditation body for hospitals. This product does not issue accreditation; the same control and evidence structure can be reused for it later.

glossary.full: National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories
glossary.text: India's accreditation body for laboratories.
An international body that accredits hospitals.
A company that processes health insurance claims for insurers. Hospitals share patient and billing data with it for cashless treatment.
A defined way for one system to exchange data with another.
The standard for sending email. Notifications can be emailed when a mail server is configured.
A standard for passing user account information between systems.
The standard used for single sign-on with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Okta.

scores.name: DPDP compliance score (requirements in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

scores.name: DPDP readiness (requirements not yet in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

scores.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

combined.name: Combined operational view
combined.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. This combines both frameworks for day-to-day tracking only. It is not a legal compliance determination and not an ISO certification result.

coverage.name: Assessment coverage (all DPDP requirements)
coverage.rule: Applicable requirements with a recorded conclusion, divided by all applicable requirements. Shows how much of the register has actually been assessed.

scores.name: DPDP compliance score (requirements in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

scores.name: DPDP readiness (requirements not yet in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

scores.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

combined.name: Combined operational view

scores.name: DPDP compliance score (requirements in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

scores.name: DPDP readiness (requirements not yet in force)
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. These requirements take effect on a future date, so this is a readiness figure and is kept apart from the in-force score.

scores.name: ISO 27001 compliance score
scores.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out.

combined.name: Combined operational view
combined.rule: Verified compliant requirements divided by applicable requirements that have been assessed, as a percentage. Partially compliant, non-compliant and not assessed requirements never count as compliant. Not applicable requirements are left out. This combines both frameworks for day-to-day tracking only. It is not a legal compliance determination and not an ISO certification result.

coverage.name: Assessment coverage (all DPDP requirements)
coverage.rule: Applicable requirements with a recorded conclusion, divided by all applicable requirements. Shows how much of the register has actually been assessed.

questions.q: A patient's relative asks at the nursing station for a copy of the patient's reports. What do you do first?
options: Hand them over, they are family
Confirm the patient has authorised it, following the hospital procedure

questions.q: Which of these is personal data?
options: The number of beds in the ward
A patient's UHID with their diagnosis

questions.q: A patient wants to withdraw consent to receive health camp messages. Who can record it?
options: It is logged as a consent withdrawal and acted on by the owner of that processing

questions.q: You sent a discharge summary to the wrong email address. What should you do?
options: Wait and see if anyone notices
Report it at once as an incident
Delete the sent mail and move on
Ask the recipient to ignore it and tell nobody

programme.title: Information security awareness for hospital staff
programme.description: Starter programme. Replace the questions with your own.

questions.q: You step away from the nursing station computer for a few minutes. What should you do?
options: Leave it, you will be back soon
Ask a visitor to watch it

questions.q: A colleague asks to use your HIS login because theirs is locked. What is correct?
options: Share it, patient care comes first
Refuse and help them get their own access restored
Write the password on a note for them
Log in for them and walk away

questions.q: An email asks you to confirm your password to keep your mailbox active. What is it most likely to be?
options: A system test you can ignore silently
